title: Reported Speech: Changing Time and Place Words — Quiz 128
content:
## Reported Speech: Changing Time and Place Words

Fill the gaps with suitable adverbs and demonstratives.

### Lesson focus

1. He said, “This is my horse.”
2. He said, “I received this letter two days ago.”
3. He said, “I'm glad to be here this evening.”

### Understand the pattern

This and here depend on where the speaker is pointing or standing. In a later report from another place, this often becomes that and here becomes there. Ago is normally measured backwards from the original speaking time, so before can be needed in the report.

### Worked answers and explanation

1. He said that that was his horse.
2. He said that he had received that letter two days before.
3. He said that he was glad to be there that evening.

If the reporter is still in the same place with the same object, this or here may remain appropriate.

### Try another

Report later, from another place: She said, 'I left this here yesterday.'

### Suggested answer

She said that she had left that there the previous day. These changes depend on the stated change of time and place.
